title: Specification of Internet Transmission Control Program
summary: The first detailed specification of the Transmission Control Program, the ancestor of TCP, published in 1974. It describes a way to send reliable streams of data between hosts across interconnected networks. It is historic, and the later specification in RFC 793 replaced this line of work. It has also been formally marked historic by RFC 7805.

eli5.summary: Imagine sending a long story by many postcards that may arrive out of order. This early plan explained how to number them and put them back right.

questions: what is the three way handshake
subtitle: The December 1974 blueprint for a program that carries reliable, ordered conversations between processes across linked networks.

tldr.problem: Processes on hosts in different packet switching networks needed a dependable way to exchange data, even though the networks in between could lose, duplicate or reorder packets.
tldr.mechanism: A Transmission Control Program on each host numbers the data, wraps it in internetwork packets, retransmits what is not acknowledged, regulates flow, and sets up connections between pairs of sockets with a three-way handshake.
tldr.outcome: This is the 1974 version of the design, now Historic and marked so by RFC 7805. It is the ancestor of the TCP used today.

today: RFC 675 is Historic and is obsoleted by RFC 7805. It records the December 1974 version of the design and is not a current specification.

sections.title: The Transmission Control Program
sections.content:
RFC 675 describes the functions of the internetwork Transmission Control Program (TCP) and its interface to the programs that use it. All network communication is treated as communication between processes, and each process may have several ports through which it talks to the ports of other processes.

Processes hand the TCP finite-length letters. The TCP breaks a letter into fragments if needed and embeds each fragment in an internetwork packet, which is in turn embedded in a local packet for the packet switching network. A gateway between networks may split a fragment into smaller ones. The TCP handles retransmission, duplicate detection, sequencing and flow control, and as a result keeps letters in order on a connection.
sections.eli5: The program works like a post office. You give it a letter, it cuts it into pieces if the road is narrow, makes sure every piece arrives, and glues the letter back together in order.

sections.title: Sockets, Connections and User Calls
sections.content:
Port names are chosen independently by each system, so the RFC joins a network identifier, a TCP identifier and a port name into a socket name that is unique across all connected networks. A pair of sockets forms a connection, which carries data in both directions.

A socket may be left partly or wholly unspecified, with the unspecified parts set to zero. A well known socket can then listen for a connection from any socket. The user-facing calls are OPEN, SEND, RECEIVE, CLOSE, INTERRUPT and STATUS. If no timeout is given, the global default is 30 seconds of retransmission before the user is notified.
sections.eli5: A socket is a full mailing address: which city, which building and which mailbox. Two addresses talking to each other make a connection, like two pen pals.

sections.title: The Internetwork Packet
sections.content:
Each internetwork packet carries a header whose length is given as 32 octets. It holds a 32-bit packet sequence number, a 32-bit acknowledgment number (the sequence number of the next octet expected), and a 16-bit window size in octets. A 16-bit control field has flags such as SYN, ACK, FIN, DSN, EOS, EOL and INT.

Addresses are written as a network address, a 16-bit TCP address and a 24-bit port address for each end. A checksum is present when the EOS bit is set. A control data octet can carry event codes or special functions such as RESET, ECHO, QUERY and STATUS.
sections.eli5: Every packet has a label with its number, which number it expects next, how much more the receiver can take, and who it is from and for.

sections.title: Opening and Closing Connections
sections.content:
Because old delayed packets can show up from earlier incarnations of a connection, the two TCPs must agree on initial sequence numbers. The RFC credits R. Tomlinson with the three way handshake and initial sequence number selection. The receiver of a first SYN cannot tell whether it is an old duplicate, so it asks the sender to verify it.

Simultaneous attempts from both sides are treated like collisions in Aloha systems: each side forgets its SYN and tries again later. A connection that has lost one end is called half-open, and it is reset when data is sent. Resynchronizing a connection is not yet specified. Closing uses a FIN control bit, and either the local user or the remote TCP can start it.
sections.eli5: Before two computers chat, they say hello, hear hello back, and say thanks. That way neither one gets fooled by an old, late message from an earlier chat.

viz.caption: THREE WAY HANDSHAKE BETWEEN TCPS A AND B (RFC 675)

messages.label: SEQ x, SYN
messages.note: A proposes its initial sequence number.

messages.label: SEQ y, SYN, ACK x+1
messages.note: B proposes its own and acknowledges A's.

messages.label: SEQ x+1, ACK y+1, data
